I have resolved the issue in [django/db/models/fields/json.py](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-q54zuf_z/django/db/models/fields/json.py).

### Summary of Changes
- Updated [`HasKeyLookup`](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-q54zuf_z/django/db/models/fields/json.py#L172-L234) (`has_key`, `has_keys`, and `has_any_keys`) to compile the final right-hand side key as a JSON object key (`."<key>"`) via [`HasKeyLookup.compile_json_path_final_key`](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-q54zuf_z/django/db/models/fields/json.py#L175-L177) rather than converting numeric strings into JSON array index paths (`[<index>]`).
- Added [`HasKeyOrArrayIndex`](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-q54zuf_z/django/db/models/fields/json.py#L257-L259) and used it in [`KeyTransformIsNull`](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-q54zuf_z/django/db/models/fields/json.py#L393-L416) and [`KeyTransformExact`](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-q54zuf_z/django/db/models/fields/json.py#L448-L485) so key transform existence checks continue to support both object keys and array indices on SQLite and Oracle.
